back: A marine animal (polyp) that secretes a calcium carbonate skeleton and, in reef-building species, lives with algae; many generations build a reef.
Algae that live in the tissues of reef-building coral, supplying food by photosynthesis in exchange for shelter and nutrients (symbiosis).
Warm water (about 23–29 °C), shallow and clear water for light, salinity of 32–36 parts per thousand, moving oxygenated water and a hard base.
Expulsion of zooxanthellae by stressed coral, usually in unusually warm water; the coral loses colour and food and may die.
A fall in the pH of sea water as it absorbs carbon dioxide, reducing carbonate ions available for skeletons and shells.
Fringing reefs grow near the shore, barrier reefs are separated by a lagoon, and atolls are rings of reef around a lagoon.
Established in 1975; rezoned in 2004 so that about a third of the park became no-take zones.
Local action can reduce pollution, fishing and damage and aid recovery, but it cannot stop warming and acidification, which need global cuts in emissions.
